goal.statement: I want to get fitter. I keep starting and stopping.
goal.near_target: Walk-jog 5 km without stopping by month 3
goal.marker: A 10 km run by the end of the year

why: I want energy for my kids in the evenings and to stop feeling out of breath on stairs.
identity: I'm someone who moves most days.

blocker.note: I start strong, miss a few days, then quit entirely.

kills: One missed day turning into a missed month
Plans that are too ambitious on day 1

history.why_stopped: Commute; missed a week when sick and never went back
Week 4 felt too hard, skipped, felt guilty

path.primary: Walk-jog intervals from home, 4+ days a week
path.fallback: Bodyweight routine indoors on rainy days
guardrails: Never increase weekly distance by more than ~10%

lanes.name: Move
starter_actions: Put shoes by the door tonight
Walk out of the door and go to the end of the street

ritual.trigger: After I put the kettle on in the morning, I put my shoes on.
ritual.warmup: Two minutes of brisk walking: always counts
ritual.minimum_day: Shoes on and walk to the end of the street and back
ritual.shutdown: Tap the chip; set shoes by the door

if_then.then: do the minimum day today; never miss twice
rest and log a note; the plan pauses, it doesn't fail

checkpoints.label: Week 4
checkpoints.ask: Is the minimum day small enough on bad days?

checkpoints.label: Month 3
checkpoints.rethink_if: fewer than 6 weekly wins → make sessions shorter, not fewer
checkpoints.ask: Is this helping, or just tracking? What would make it easier?

surviving_habit: Shoes on after the kettle, every morning

first_action.text: Put your shoes by the door right now

compass:
WHY: energy for the kids, stairs without gasping.
HOW: walk-jog from home after the kettle, 4+ days a week. A missed day is normal; missing twice is the only thing to avoid.
PIVOT: if it feels hard 3 weeks running, shorten sessions; never quit the shoes-on habit.
